3. Appellant Nos. 1-5 herein, the heirs of Zahiruddin as defendant Nos. 1-5 and appellant Nos. 5-11 as defendant Nos. 14-20 contested the suit by filing two separate written statements contending similar facts. In their written statements the defendants contended that Raisuddin Sheikh and others were the tenants under the admitted landlord. The defendants admitted the auction purchase of the suit land by the predecessor of the plaintiffs as stated in the plaint. The defendants also admitted the claim of mortgaging the suit land with their predecessor and execution of the deed of re-conveyance. The defendants denied that the mortgagors returned back the money within time and the mortgagee on receipt of the money delivered back the possession of the suit land to the mortgagors. The defendants asserted that the suit was barred by limitation. 

 4. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Pirganj by his judgment and decree dated 30-4-2005 decreed the suit on the findings, inter-alia, that the predecessor of the defendants during his life time delivered back possession of the suit land to the predecessor of the plaintiffs on receipt of the money paid for the mortgage and the successors of the mortgagors have been enjoying and possessing the suit land; once a mortgage always a mortgage and limitation for filing a suit for redemption of mortgage being 60 years, the suit having been filed within 51 years, the same was not barred by limitation and the plaintiffs were entitled to redeem the mortgage; the suit having been filed under rule 1 of Order XXXIV of the Code of Civil Procedure, section 95 A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act) cannot be a bar for redemption of the mortgaged property even if the transaction in question became past and closed. 

 "V. For that the High Court Division erred in law and facts by holding on the principle of 'once a mortgage always a mortgage', that the respondents are entitled to the redemption for getting back the suit land by setting aside the finding of the Appellate Court that the transaction under a sale deed of 1947 with a condition to re-convey if payment is made within 5 years being a usufructuary mortgage it became a past and closed transaction in terms of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 inasmuch as the period of 7 years was over long before, 1972. 

 7. Mr. Moinul Hossain, learned Counsel, appearing for the appellants has reiterated the grounds on which leave was granted. In support of his submissions, he placed the plaint, the written statement, the depositions of the witnesses. 

 11. The Appellate Court being the last Court of fact considering the evidence in detail came to the finding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case by examining the competent witnesses whereas, the defendants proved their case as made out in the written statement. The Appellate Court came to the further finding that the trial Court ought to have decided that the plaintiffs suit without prayer for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession was not maintainable in law. The Appellate Court also found that the trial Court on wrong interpretation of the witnesses of the plaintiffs came to the wrong finding that the price of the suit land was returned back to the plaintiffs predecessor. The Appellate Court further came to the finding that as per their own case, the mortgage having been redeemed 46 years ago, the trial Court erred in decreeing the suit. 

 12. We have gone through the plaint as well as the depositions of the witnesses. In the plaint, the plaintiffs specifically stated that their predecessor, Ahmed Ali returned back the entire money of the mortgage deed to the defendants predecessor, Zahiruddin and then he delivered back the possession of the suit land on the talk (in Bangla, it has been stated as "কথা হয়") that subsequently, he would execute a deed of reconveyance, in the meantime, he (Zahiruddin) died for which he could not execute and register a deed of reconveyance. 

 13. A reading of the plaint as a whole, in fact, shows that the plaintiffs wanted to have a kabala from the defendants as a proof of the redemption of the mortgage which took place within 5 (five) years from the date of mortgage, but in the four corners of the plaint, no date has been mentioned on which date, the mortgage money was returned back to the mortgagee, but in the deposition of PW 1, he stated that the money was returned back to the mortgagee, again no specific mention of date, but in cross-examination, PW 1 stated that the money was returned back on 1st Asar, 1963 (it is not clear whether BS or AD). None of the PWs supported the case of the plaintiffs that the mortgagor returned back the money to the mortgagee. Even for argument's sake, it is conceded that the mortgage money was returned and the possession of the suit land was given back to the mortgagor, then the mortgage was, in fact, redeemed, and in that case the only remedy that remained opened to the plaintiffs was to file a suit for specific performance of contract within the period of limitation, because as per the own case of the plaintiffs with the return of the mortgage money as well as the delivery of possession nothing remained to be redeemed, instead they filed the suit for redemption of the mortgage. It is very significant to note that in the plaint, the cause of action has been shown to have arisen on 1-1-1996, when defendant Nos. 1-4 demanded the suit land from plaintiff No. 1 and then on 1-11-1998 when the said defendant refused to execute and register the deed of reconveyance in their favour, but in the prayer of the plaint, the plaintiffs simply prayed for a decree for redemption of the mortgaged land.
